item.title: I escaped
item.description: Frinklepuff couldn't contain me for long
item.content:encoded:
I managed to escape my imprisonment and am now hiding in a homemade shelter in the dark forest.

I think Frinklepuff and his fellow gnomes lost the trail 2 days ago, but I’ve been laying low to be safe. I’m always nervous that I might see a pointy red hat turn the corner. If I am captured again they might by chance discover my weakness and put me in a hole so deep and dank that no one will ever find me.

I saw Wildwood. It was great! All around 10/10 film. Very dark though. I was not expecting it to be quite as gory and violent as it ended up being. But fantastic. Real Narnia / Alice in Wonderland vibes.

Anyways, I’ve made friends with one of the dryads here. She’s been keeping me hidden under her branches, which is the shelter I mentioned before. I may voyage out for food in a few hours if I don’t hear any spritely giggling.

Until then,

Jack

item.title: the state of things...
item.content:encoded:
I was buried under a mountain of gnomes yesterday, which is why you didn’t receive my letter.

The gnomes bound me in powerful chains made from the meat of a dandelion and the whispers of tigers. Gnomes are crafty, they know that no mortal bonds could contain me.

Anyways, Wildwood is out in theaters now and I’m going to see it on Sunday. I’ve heard good things about the longest stop-motion film ever made, which took 19 years. The animation looks beautiful and the story sounds hype.

And in other news I recently published a short story on my website, check it out.

Oh no… the gnomes heard me. Frincklepuff is coming to tighten my bonds.

My next missive may take a while. I’ll try to sneak a letter in a bottle out the next time they go to defend the Myrwood.

Until then,

Jack

item.title: A Few Interesting Books
item.content:encoded:
Recently I’ve gotten really into weird fiction / cosmic horror as a genre, so here are some recommendations:

  1. There is no Antimemetics Division by qntm
    • This book was originally a series of short stories from the SMP Foundation. It’s fantastic.
  2. The Fisherman by John Langan
  3. The Hike by Drew Magary
    • Really bizzare story of a guy who tries to go on a short hike which ends up lasting decades
  4. Blacktail by Scott Hawkins
    • What if God wasn’t human?
  5. Slow Gods by Claire North
  6. City of Stairs by Robert Jackson Bennet
  7. A Short Stay in Hell by Steven L. Peck

They are amazing! Also, if you haven’t already, read the Cradle series by Will Wight.
